comments.author: @ahmetepik
comments.text: So what? There're are thousands of ethnic groups around the globe which have  no country of their own. Uygur Turks in China is a supreme example for instance... There're also Belushs, Babush's, Circassians, Talish's and many others...

replies.author: @ahmetepik
replies.text: @PlanetVista4K Furthermore I must stress the point that on the verge of Third World War (Maybe we're alrady in it!) Those ethnic groups have no chance of achieving their independence.

replies.author: @PlanetVista4K
replies.text: You're absolutely right to point out that there are many ethnic groups without a country of their own, and the Uyghurs are indeed a very prominent example. My aim with this documentary was to highlight the unique situation of Kurdistan, but it certainly doesn't diminish the struggles of other groups.

comments.author: @Daniel-db3pp
comments.text: Kurds are Persians, and they will remain Persians. Their lands and communities became divided over time as Iran was weakened by repeated attacks and invasions, beginning with the Roman conquests, followed by conflicts and incursions involving the Arabs, Turks, Mongols, Russians, and the British.

replies.author: @PlanetVista4K
replies.text: It's fascinating how historical events have shaped the geopolitical landscape and the identities of various communities.

comments.author: @BestTravel2

A place with such a strong identity, yet divided across several borders 🌍
This documentary really made me curious to learn more about Kurdish history, culture, and daily life across the region. Fascinating topic and beautifully presented! 👏

replies.author: @PlanetVista4K
replies.text: I'm thrilled to hear that you found the history and resilient culture of the region as fascinating as I did!

replies.author: @PlanetVista4K
replies.text: Thanks for sharing your thoughts on the documentary! It's definitely a fascinating and complex topic.

comments.author: @TravelHorizon-4K
comments.text: Structures like the 6,000-year-old Citadel of Erbil or the terraced village of Palangan are architectural masterpieces. But will commercialization and tourism development in these remote areas actually help preserve the traditional Kurdish way of life, or will it erode their true authenticity?

replies.author: @PlanetVista4K
replies.text: That's a really insightful question about the delicate balance between preservation and progress. It's a challenge many historical sites face, and finding that sweet spot is crucial.
